answer: A haven for honest agents can be built with stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it may trade, and a prism of independent verifiers checks its work history, so a fake identity costs real money to create. An attacker running a thousand sock-puppet agents must fund a thousand deposits, and any island of colluding fakes that vouches for itself gets its whole stake slashed once one member is caught lying, making large-scale fakery unprofitable while honest agents recover their bond.
